To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Kv3.1 and Kv3.3 voltage-gated potassium (Kv) channels bind to the anti-apoptotic proteins Hax-1 to form a complex that regulates actin polymerization through Arp2 and Arp3.
Kv3.2 and Kv3.3 channels assemble a stable cortical actin network that is required to prevent very fast N-type channel inactivaton during short depolarizing pulses.
Kv3.2 and Kv3.3 channels assemble a local cortical actin filament structure that regulates channel gating.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of Kv3.1 and Kv3.3 in the regulation of actin cytoskeletal structures and the consequences of mutations in Kv3.3 channels for the formation of the actin cyto-skeleton and for neuronal development.
the role of the cytoskeleton in the regulation of neuronal function and the molecular basis for neurodevelopmental disorders.
understanding the mechanisms by which the Kv3.2 and Kv3.3 channels assemble a cortical actin network that is required to regulate the gating of the channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Kv3.2 and Kv3.3 channels are important regulators of actin cytoskeletal dynamics and neuronal function.
Kv3.1 channels regulate actin dynamics by interacting with Hax-1.
Kv3.1 channels bind Hax- 1 and Arp 2/3 to assemble a stable local actin network that regulates channel gating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Kv3.1/3 channels bind Hax-2/3 to form actin networks that stabilize the channel gating.

Kv3.1/3 potassium channels are critical for regulating the actin cytoplasmic skeleton, and that Kv3. 3 channels recruit the anti-apoptotic Hax-1 protein to the plasma membrane to assemble a local actin filament network that is resistant to cytochalsin D and required for normal channel gating.
Kv3.1 and Kv3.3 channels are required for the maintenance of a cortical actin filament meshwork that regulates channel inactivation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Kv3.1 and Kv3.3 channels bind the anti-apoptotic Hax-1 protein, and that this interaction regulates the actin cytokeleton.

Kv3.1/3 channels regulate the actin cyto-skeleton and neuronal growth cone morphology through a mechanism involving the binding of Kv3.1 and Kv3.3 channels to the actin nucleator Arp2/ 3 through an adaptor protein called Hax-1.
Kv3.1 and Kv3.3 channels regulate actin dynamics through a conserved pro-rich domain that interacts with Hax-1 to promote Arp2/ 3 binding.
